title: Improve quantized inference kernel performance: INT8/FP8 optimizations, smoothquant and dequant fusion paths
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: customer workloads (long conversational contexts + embedding-heavy reranking) showed that quantized model paths (INT8/FP8) are not consistently delivering expected cost/latency gains for small batch/latency-sensitive inference. Root causes: (1) separate dequantize -> GEMM -> quantize paths causing excessive memory traffic, (2) scheduler picks FP16 kernels for some shapes due to static heuristics, and (3) KV-cache handling didn't account for scale factors introduced by smoothquant-style per-channel scaling, leading to extra ops.

This PR implements several coordinated runtime changes to improve quantized inference throughput and latency while keeping functional parity and safe fallbacks: (1) fused dequantize+GEMM kernel for INT8/FP8 backends to eliminate intermediate full-precision buffers and reduce memory bandwidth, (2) dequant-fusion codegen path that emits a single kernel when model quant params and layout match the fusion preconditions, (3) smoothquant-aware compiler pass: detect per-channel scales (and optional bias-correction) and bake them into weight transforms during compile/prepare step instead of on-the-fly per-request, (4) dynamic kernel selector updates: runtime now prefers quantized fused kernels for shapes where benchmarks show win; selector uses microbench histogram from recent traffic to avoid regressions, (5) scheduler hint for continuous batching to coalesce quantized requests and avoid mixing quantized/unquantized batches, and (6) KV-cache compatibility: KV cache continues to store cached keys/values in FP16 but we apply scale metadata and on-load fast-path to avoid runtime dequant/req quant cycles.

Notable design choices: fusion is conservative — only enabled when weights are row-major and scale factors are per-output-channel; otherwise runtime falls back to existing dequant->gemm path. Smoothquant scaling is applied at model-load time if the model manifest includes quantization metadata (we add a codec for optional metadata in the model registry). The kernel implements the fused dequant+GEMM in CUDA with attention to mmapped weight buffers and prefetching; we keep a portable C++ reference path for CPU and as a correctness check.

Performance: microbench results (internal perf harness) on A100: INT8 fused path reduces end-to-end token latency by ~18-26% for seq_len=512, batch=1 compared to previous INT8 implementation; throughput improvements of 1.3-1.6x for typical batch sizes (1-8). FP8 (8e4) fused path shows 12-20% latency wins vs prior FP8 dequantized path. Memory working set reduced by ~30% on average for large models due to removed intermediate buffers.

Compatibility & safety: feature gated behind runtime config flag quant_fusion.enabled=false by default for rollout. We added a runtime supervisor check that compares new kernel latency vs baseline on a small sampled traffic set before switching traffic to fused path. No model format breaking changes: metadata is optional.

Testing: unit tests for fused kernels correctness (bit-exact within tolerance vs reference FP32 path), integration tests for scheduler/coalescing, regression tests for CLI-based model load, and extended e2e perf harness runs. CI: added new perf job quant-kernel-smoke which runs lightweight microbenchmarks on GPU runners.

Related Linear items: ENG-1824 (quant kernel project), ENG-1899 (smoothquant compiler pass), ENG-1951 (scheduler batching hints).

Summary of what changed: small delta in many runtime files: kernel impls, codegen, kernel selector heuristics, scheduler hints, KV-cache metadata plumbing, tests, and perf harness glue.

How to validate locally: follow docs/redwood/inference/quantization/README.md added in this PR. Quick sanity: ./bazel run //serving/runtime:quant-kernel-smoke -- --model tests/models/quant/small.bin --mode smoke

Release notes: Speedups for quantized models (INT8/FP8) via fused dequant+GEMM kernels, smoothquant compile-time transforms, and improved kernel selection/scheduling. Opt-in via quant_fusion.enabled until staged rollout completes.
